contract: generate(model) -> list of rows. model = {'name': str, 'strength': t, 'values': [v_0, ..., v_{k-1}], 'forbidden': [[[p, level], ...], ...]}: parameter p takes a level in 0..v_p-1 and each forbidden entry lists parameter-level pairs that must not all occur in one row. Return a list of rows, each a list of k Python ints. Every row must avoid all forbidden combinations, and the rows together must contain every combination of levels of t distinct parameters that occurs in at least one valid configuration (the evaluator decides feasibility exactly). Score: number of rows, minimised; an array that misses a feasible combination or contains a forbidden one is invalid. generate() runs in a sandboxed subprocess (no files, network or subprocesses; CPU limit 60 s for pairwise and 120 s for 3-way tasks, 2 GB); it should be deterministic (seed any randomness, do not read clocks).
notes: Models and constraints are the CASA-format files of the ICSE 2015 CIT benchmark archive (Zenodo 581657); their 1-based level numbers are converted to 0-based. Feasible t-way combinations are decided exactly at preparation time (backtracking search); an independent Z3 recomputation agreed on every required combination of all five models (validation/software-checks.json), hence recreated_verified. The candidate gets a fixed CPU budget in a Python sandbox, unlike the published C++ solvers (1000 s to 5 h per run), so sizes are comparable with the published values but run times are not.
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: Software engineering: 3-way covering array for the SPIN simulator model
description: Build a smallest 3-way covering array for the 18-option SPIN model-checker simulator model under its forbidden option combinations. Every feasible triple of option settings must appear in some test configuration; fewer configurations is better.
benchmark: Software engineering: 3-way covering array for the SPIN simulator model
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Cohen, Dwyer and Shi (TSE 2008): constrained interaction testing of highly configurable systems; introduces the SPIN, GCC, Apache and Bugzilla constraint models and a SAT-checked greedy construction.
Jia, Cohen, Harman and Petke (ICSE 2015): hyperheuristic search for constrained covering arrays; publishes the benchmark archive used here.
ICSE15_HHSA_Benchmarks.zip (CC BY 4.0): CASA-format model and constraint files; levels are numbered from 1.
Lin, Cai, Luo, Lin and Zhang (FastCA, ESEC/FSE 2019): state-of-the-art local search for constrained covering arrays; Table 5 lists 3-way sizes on these models.

limitations: Published sizes: FastCA, TCA and HHSA reach 80 rows and CASA 94 rows (FastCA, ESEC/FSE 2019, Table 5, 1000 s). FastCA used CASA's constraint files, which are logically equivalent to the archive's for SPIN-S (checked with Z3). The counting lower bound is 64.
The array size is the only objective; generation time is bounded by the sandbox CPU limit and is not scored, whereas the published solvers ran for 1000 s to 5 h in C++.
Feasible combinations are decided by an exact search at preparation time and cross-checked with Z3 in the tests; a Z3 disagreement would change the required set.
The models are public; a candidate could embed a precomputed array. Scores are comparable with published sizes only for arrays generated within the contract.

papers.title: Software engineering research: source-based research tasks

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Combinatorial interaction testing of configurable software: choose as few test configurations as possible such that every feasible combination of t option settings is exercised, while respecting constraints that forbid some option combinations.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Configurable systems such as compilers, web servers and model checkers have astronomically many configurations; interaction faults are triggered by a few options together, so smaller constrained covering arrays reduce testing cost while keeping the interaction coverage guarantee. Constraint handling is a central open difficulty because invalid configurations cannot be executed.

papers.title: Constructing Interaction Test Suites for Highly-Configurable Systems in the Presence of Constraints: A Greedy Approach
papers.primary_goal: Generate small interaction test suites (constrained covering arrays) for real configurable software whose options are restricted by constraints.
papers.task_relation: The task asks for the same object, a constrained t-way covering array, on configuration models introduced in this paper (SPIN, GCC, Apache).
